Control procedure name: Monthly reconciliation of the procurement plan
Detailed control procedure description:
OBJECTIVE — Confirm that the approved plan reflects purchasing activity and authorised changes.
WHO — Procurement Analyst.
WHEN / TRIGGER — Monthly after period end: Procurement Analyst extracts transactional records and reconciles them to the approved procurement plan, including status and planned dates.
IF PASSED — If matched: document reconciliation and obtain approval of the updated plan.
IF EXCEPTION — If not matched: consult business initiators, document postponed or cancelled items, update the plan and obtain approval before publication.
RESULT — Result: current approved plan consistent with procurement records.
CONTROL TRAIL — Trace: versioned plan, source export, difference log, initiator response and approver sign-off.
Governing internal policy or directive: Procurement Policy and Delegation of Authority (illustrative)
Evidence of control execution: Versioned procurement plan; source export; discrepancy log; approver sign-off.
Overall assessment (details): Anonymised educational example; operating effectiveness has not been tested.

OBJECTIVE — Identify adverse changes affecting active suppliers.
WHO — Third-Party Risk Analyst.
WHEN / TRIGGER — Monthly: the Third-Party Risk Analyst checks the active supplier population for insolvency, liquidation, trading restrictions and defined risk alerts.
IF PASSED — If clear: record the nil-exception review.
IF EXCEPTION — If flagged: document the event, escalate to relevant business, legal or finance owners and track their decision.
RESULT — Result: a reviewed and distributed supplier risk report.
CONTROL TRAIL — Trace: dated screening export, exception list, escalation and decision record.
Evidence of control execution: Supplier screening export; reviewed exception list; escalation and management decision.

Detailed control procedure description:
OBJECTIVE — Verify ledger cash data against independent bank evidence.
WHO — Finance Accountant.
WHEN / TRIGGER — At month-end: the Finance Accountant obtains all active-account statements, including accounts with no movement, and compares opening and closing balances and receipts/payments with ledger extracts.
IF PASSED — If matched: sign the reconciliation and submit it for independent review.
IF EXCEPTION — If unmatched: investigate entries, make authorised corrections, document unresolved items and escalate them.
RESULT — Result: a completed cash-account reconciliation.
CONTROL TRAIL — Trace: statements, ERP export, reconciliation, exception log and reviewer checklist.
Evidence of control execution: Bank statements; ERP reconciliation; exception register; signed review checklist.

Control procedure name: Reconciliation of billing data to the financial ledger
Detailed control procedure description:
OBJECTIVE — Confirm that billing entries are completely and accurately reflected in the finance ledger.
WHO — Revenue Accountant.
WHEN / TRIGGER — After the monthly billing interface run: the Revenue Accountant compares billing extracts against ERP revenue totals by service category and period.
IF PASSED — If matched: record a nil-exception reconciliation and have the checklist reviewed.
IF EXCEPTION — If different: consult the billing process owner, initiate an authorised correction and repeat the reconciliation; unresolved items remain open and escalated.
RESULT — Result: an evidence-backed billing-to-ledger reconciliation.
CONTROL TRAIL — Trace: source exports, worksheet, exception correspondence and signed review.
Evidence of control execution: Billing export; ERP revenue report; reconciliation worksheet; reviewer sign-off.

Control procedure name: Reconciliation of warehouse and accounting records
Detailed control procedure description:
OBJECTIVE — Identify discrepancies between warehouse and financial inventory records.
WHO — Inventory Accountant.
WHEN / TRIGGER — At month-end: the Inventory Accountant compares item-level quantities and balances across warehouse and accounting reports.
IF PASSED — If matched: save the reconciled comparison and obtain review sign-off.
IF EXCEPTION — If different: query the warehouse owner, trace supporting receipts/movements, process approved corrections and rerun the comparison.
RESULT — Result: reconciled records or an explicit open-exception list.
CONTROL TRAIL — Trace: comparison report, source extracts, correction approvals and reviewer confirmation.
Evidence of control execution: Item-level variance report; source extracts; correction approvals; review evidence.

Control procedure name: Restriction of changes to closed accounting periods
Detailed control procedure description:
OBJECTIVE — Prevent unauthorised modifications to a closed reporting period.
WHO — ERP System Control.
WHEN / TRIGGER — Whenever a transaction is submitted: the ERP checks period status and user permissions before processing.
IF PASSED — If the period is open and the user is authorised: the standard posting proceeds.
IF EXCEPTION — If the period is closed or privileges are insufficient: block the posting and require an authorised exception / reopening workflow.
RESULT — Result: closed-period integrity is protected.
CONTROL TRAIL — Trace: system configuration, rejection logs and authorised exception approvals.
Governing internal policy or directive: Financial Close and Access Management Procedure (illustrative)
Evidence of control execution: ERP configuration; system log; change or access ticket; authorisation evidence.
